name: JSX (white with red X)
description: White all over. A large red X (the JSX mark) just behind the forward door, a small 'JSX' under the cockpit, and 'JSX' on the engine nacelles with the J and S in grey and the X in red. On the fin a red V high up and a red inverted V below it, as an X pulled apart at its middle; the lower V's forward arm runs on down across the tail cone. A thin red line edges the fin's leading edge and runs along the belly to a red nose tip. A red band along the top of the wings.

titles.style: The JSX wordmark: thin, widely spaced geometric capitals, J and S in grey, the X in red as the mark's two crossing strokes; on the nacelle's side, reading normally on both.
Small, thin spaced capitals under the cockpit's side window, ahead of the door.

logos.description: The JSX X: two red strokes crossing, a little narrower than tall, over the first cabin window just behind the forward door.
The same X on the right, ahead of the service door (placed by eye on a three-quarter view).

notes: Drawn on N963JX (ERJ-145, 2026-05-02); the ERJ-135s wear it the same way (N253JX). The fin's red V and inverted V are one X pulled apart at its middle; the inverted V's forward arm runs off the fin down across the tail cone to about y -0.4. The forward X spans y -0.29 to 0.72 at x 0.217 (about 1.5 m tall). The thin red edging also runs along the dorsal fillet and round the tailplane's tips and edges; the fillet's and tailplane's are not drawn. The belly line's height is read off photos from below and is uncertain; the wing band's place on the chord is from oblique views (low). Some jets fly a plainer version (N266JX, 2026-04-24: no forward X, no engine titles, no edging) and some wear specials (N247JX 'This Is How We Fly' in red, N960JX retro JetSuiteX, N242JX 'Club JSX'); not drawn here. The 'from' year is left out: no dated source in hand.
history: New in the LAX round (2026-11-20); JSX had no scheme here before.
